newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zairean rebels capture town, advance.
newsitem.headline: Zairean rebels capture town, advance.

text.p: Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila said on Wednesday his forces had captured the northwestern town of Isiro, after heavy fighting, and were moving towards Buta, 450 km (280 miles) east of Gbadolite, the jungle palace of ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko.
Kabila said retreating government troops backed by foreign mercenaries had withdrawn to Buta, the next stop towards Mobutu's multi-million-dollar residence.

Kabila, head of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL), said Isiro which was also used as a counter-offensive base by mercenaries recruited by Zaire's embattled government, fell late on Tuesday.
"Our forces are now in complete control of Isiro. The town was taken late on Tuesday," he said.

Kabila, waging Africa's latest rebellion, said government forces backed by MI-24 (Hind) Russian-built attack helicopters and war planes earlier bombarded rebel positions around the town of Lubutu, a gateway to the city of Kisangani.
Kisangani, Zaire's third largest city, is the main base for government troops and foreign mercenaries seeking to reverse Kabila's stunning battlefield victories in the last four months.
